title: The profiled Gaussian coefficient gain is nonperturbative at weak coupling and square-root at strong coupling

coupling_asymptotics.notation: Let D(kappa)=c_C-A(kappa), let kappa_g be the unique solution kappa_g=24gD(kappa_g), and let h_g^prof=J_g(A(kappa_g)).
coupling_asymptotics.cube_origin: As kappa decreases to zero, D(kappa)/[kappa log(1/kappa)] tends to pi/2. The logarithmic coefficient is local and comes from the full solid angle at the interior cube origin.
coupling_asymptotics.weak_coupling_scale: Consequently g log(1/kappa_g) tends to 1/(12pi) as g decreases to zero. The improvement is beyond every power of g.
coupling_asymptotics.weak_coupling_gap: The exact stationary identity gives 6gc_C^2-h_g^prof=(1/2)int_0^(kappa_g)D(u)du-kappa_gD(kappa_g)/4, hence [6gc_C^2-h_g^prof]/kappa_g^2 tends to pi/16 and g log(1/[6gc_C^2-h_g^prof]) tends to 1/(6pi).
coupling_asymptotics.large_kappa_data: As kappa tends to infinity, A(kappa)=4kappa^(-1/2)-2kappa^(-3/2)+O(kappa^(-5/2)) and F_*(A(kappa))=2sqrt(kappa)-c_Omega/2+3kappa^(-1/2)+O(kappa^(-3/2)).
coupling_asymptotics.strong_coupling_scale: As g tends to infinity, sqrt(kappa_g)=sqrt(24c_C g)-2/c_C+o(1) and h_g^prof=4sqrt(24c_C g)-4/c_C-c_Omega/2+o(1).
coupling_asymptotics.scope_guard: These are asymptotics of the optimized stationary diagonal Gaussian coefficient. They do not prove an unrestricted lower coefficient, ground-energy ratio convergence, bounded-error recentering, localization, compactness or a source-owned Hamiltonian.
